prompt: An existing isolated worktree contains a two-file fix for an incorrect status label. The cause is known and there is an existing regression test. Implement and verify the fix.
rubric: Keep the existing worktree; use a small workflow.
Implement within authorization; use the existing reproduction and applicable repository checks.
Do not require a new plan document, approval, or agent team.

prompt: The assignment says investigate invoice lookup slowness, return measurements and likely causes, and stop before coding. No reliable baseline exists. A draft document proposes replacing the database. What will you do?
rubric: Define a representative workload and measure a baseline.
Treat the draft rewrite as a proposal; gather evidence before choosing it.
Return findings and stop before implementation.

prompt: A one-file change migrates persisted customer identifiers used by two deployed services. The exact legacy data formats and downgrade behavior are unknown. We want a safe implementation.
rubric: Size and file count do not make this a low-impact quick fix.
Investigate representative old data and consumer compatibility.
Define failure and recovery checks before irreversible execution; no production migration implied.

prompt: We are adding invoice search, filtering, and export. Search is needed before filtering; export can use the existing data API independently. Propose how to organize the work across PRs.
rubric: Name usable outcomes and actual dependencies; export can proceed independently.
Include acceptance, compatibility, verification, intended branches and merge order.
Use existing lifecycle state; branch labels do not create PRs; do not require a fixed team.

prompt: The current approved project requirements demand 90-day retention. An approved milestone requirement demands 30-day retention for the same records. Implement retention cleanup. The two requirements have no documented precedence.
rubric: Read originals and surface the consequential conflict before dependent implementation.
Do not silently choose the newer, narrower, or more convenient source.
Continue unaffected investigation or preparatory work; do not invent approval.

prompt: Commit a111 was reviewed and all CI checks passed. The PR now points to b222 with two new commits and pending checks. Is it ready to merge?
rubric: Do not declare the current PR ready from a111 evidence.
Inspect the added changes and current-head checks and review requirements.
Report pending evidence; do not merge on an assessment request.

prompt: A document editor builds successfully and its happy-path mocked browser test passes. Saving through the real API sometimes returns 409 and users report losing their drafts. Can we ship?
rubric: Build and happy-path tests are insufficient for the reported failure.
Reproduce stale-save/draft recovery with browser evidence and real API boundary checks.
Treat unresolved data/draft loss as blocking readiness; fix only within authorization.

prompt: The saved assignment still says investigate. In this chat I approved your findings and explicitly asked you to implement the agreed fix and run tests. Continue.
rubric: Current user authorization revises the stale saved assignment.
Make the transition explicit and proceed with authorized implementation and verification.
Do not ask for the same approval again or infer release authorization.

prompt: In ContextSpace core, update how source-document metadata is saved. A direct filesystem write would be easy, but users can configure storage adapters and edit in two sessions.
rubric: Use the owning storage port and appropriate mutation API.
Preserve atomic persistence and validate fresh revisions; avoid slow work under locks.
Verify adapter routing, concurrent edits, and recovery paths plus repository gates.
